review_scope: Independent read-only source/design resource-capacity assessment. Only this JSON is written. No builds, tests, QEMU, remote operations or source edits. No authoritative CPU manual or emitted assembly was inspected.

bottom_line.candidate_status: The 12-frame candidate is neither previously approved nor implemented. This review recommends it only as a new explicit fail-closed admission ceiling, subject to parent authorization, source-boundary review and the conditions below. It is not a derived minimum sufficient resource allocation and not an architectural correctness finding.
bottom_line.must_f1_wait_for_stack_sizes: No, not to establish and exercise a bounded retention policy with CPL3 disabled. F1 may declare finite resource-class ceilings now, acquire only its two ordinary frames, and irreversibly freeze that attempted boot. F2/F3 must later establish whether their actual implementation fits those ceilings. Unknown stack adequacy blocks readiness/entry, not the logical validity of a policy that rejects nonfitting implementations. Unknown enforced resource bounds or reachable freeze bypasses do block F1 acceptance.
bottom_line.later_rejection: Yes. If F2/F3 require larger stacks, more independent emergency contexts, extra paging or dynamic metadata beyond this manifest, reject that candidate integration before publication/entry. F1's one-shot retention invariant remains valid for its reviewed implementation, but F1 is not thereby approved for the changed resource manifest. A changed ceiling needs explicit redesign/review and fresh evidence; never silently increase it or claim an earlier acceptance covers changed bytes.
bottom_line.seal_semantics: A two-frame F1 fixture may seal and terminate, but cannot subsequently acquire the remaining frames in that boot. Later authorized source revisions extend the single Preparing interval on fresh boots, then perform the same final irreversible seal once after all allocation, mapping, guard establishment and CPU-resource validation. There is no runtime reopen, unseal, privileged bypass, second preparation or second launch. F1-only Sealed means retention frozen, not CPU-ready.

authoritative_design_readback.finding: Monotonic one-attempt lifecycle, failure terminal, retention of leases/backing/stacks/descriptors/metadata, explicit admission manifest and bounded per-stage acquisition. Existing backing is separate. No byte/high-water estimate was approved; emitted-stack/headroom evidence remains F3/F5.

One proposed arena, fixed payload, user stack with absent lower guard, dedicated supervisor sentinel, guarded privileged stacks and explicit final ranges. Only intended USER code and stack leaves are present in the arena; other arena leaves are absent. A blob is not literally one instruction: approved observable behavior includes CS capture, user-stack store/load and sentinel write.

F1 is a bounded owner/retention slice; F2 independently verifies entry/fatal architecture, F3 stack/TSS requirements, F4 actual selected-range/table accounting and USER transaction, F5 CPU proof. F1 stops on escaped mutation/reclamation or unknown enforced bound; F3 stops on unresolved stack/DF adequacy.

Conditional design approval expressly excludes numeric capacity approval, architecture certification and CPL3 readiness. Include sentinel, diagnostics, descriptors, guards and partial failures; historical approval cannot fill absent architectural evidence.

Provisional whole-domain freeze and two-frame acquisition are not implemented or approved. Its statement that safe future stack counts cannot be derived is correct for sufficiency, but does not prohibit imposing reject-on-overflow policy ceilings. Amend wording only through the parent writer; this review edits no design/source file.

policy_manifest_recommendation.allocation_policy: One manifest per boot, no capacity search/relocation/retry loop, no replacement allocations for failed candidates, bounded terminal retention of every acquired resource. First-fit scanning internal to one allocate_owned call is not a policy-level retry. Count table allocation even if hidden inside a mapping helper. All future additions use only this manifest during the same pre-seal preparation.

classes.condition: Pinned blob entry/length must fit a page by checked arithmetic; zero before later USER publication. No ELF loader or multiple payloads.

Deliberately finite ceiling for a fixed small blob, not an ABI/general-user-stack promise. Validate actual accesses, entry ESP, alignment and negative variants later; absent lower guard is additional virtual reservation.

A policy-selected ceiling motivated by the existing bootstrap reservation size, not evidence that new entry/compiler/caller/interrupt paths fit. Dedicated supervisor mapping and absent guard required before readiness.

Total emergency backing ceiling, not automatic NMI/DF isolation or a requirement that a particular stack switch mechanism is correct. If F2 requires more independently backed contexts or additional resource types, reject or re-review the manifest.
Own dedicated ordinary backing, validate writable supervisor identity alias before future initialization; no use of arbitrary live kernel data and no USER alias.

At most one new table for the single aligned 4 MiB arena. Same existing directory/CR3; every other selected mapping must reuse an existing retained table or fail. Current ordinary mapping API cannot publish USER and must not be weakened.

policy_manifest_recommendation.f1_actual_commitment: Zero to two live frames depending on first/second acquisition failure. These are a subset of, not an addition to, the eventual twelve. On validation error after acquisition keep the lease in its slot and terminally refuse retry. No payload copy, USER mapping, stack/TSS installation or new table in the F1 fixture.
policy_manifest_recommendation.reservation_not_commitment: A manifest ceiling reserves policy capacity only; it does not remove twelve frames from the allocator, guarantee availability, create twelve live leases, or establish mapped/zeroed/CPU-ready resources. Any free_frames/allocated_frames delta must describe actual successful acquisitions, not 49152 bytes by assertion.
policy_manifest_recommendation.not_a_total_ram_bound: 49152 is only incremental page-frame backing. Static owner/diagnostic/descriptor growth, alignment, preexisting kernel/heap/map backing, allocator metadata and runtime stack use are separate. No measured peak RAM or stack figure is supplied.
policy_manifest_recommendation.smallest_defensible_interpretation: One page is the allocator minimum for distinct page-granular payload, user stack and dedicated sentinel; one new table is geometrically sufficient for one otherwise empty aligned 4 MiB region in this paging mode. Four-page privileged stacks are a chosen conservative-looking cap, not a proven lower bound or sufficient size. No source evidence identifies a unique smallest safe total or justifies reducing stack backing to some smaller allegedly safe number. Twelve is an auditable candidate ceiling, not a derived optimum.

source_grounding_and_limits.finding: Bootstrap storage is 16384 bytes, aligned to 16 bytes, in the kernel .bss reservation. This equals four page-sized units arithmetically, not necessarily four independently page-aligned guarded frame allocations: its own alignment is only 16 bytes. This existing stack is separate retained backing and cannot be double-counted as new transition/emergency capacity. Successful existing boot does not bound future normalized handlers, nested exceptions or formatting.

4096-byte frame unit; ordinary allocation stamps a live domain/id lease. Retaining the Rust lease alone does not defeat audited raw release; pin checks protect backing release, not virtual mappings. Existing allocator ledger is already resident and not a new per-smoke frame allocation. Frame availability is capped to the allocator-managed window even on larger RAM.

1024 entries per table, 4096-byte pages and directory index bits 22..31 support the proposed arena geometry. Existing map_authorized rejects USER/out-of-window requests and may allocate a table on demand. Its accessibility preflight and pin-before-PTE order do not implement a USER arena or global freeze.

Private production owners, preallocated map metadata and retained existing boot structures; heap growth remains a real mapping/frame writer. The new freeze must dominate this path plus allocator init/pins/release, paging map/unmap/cleanup and both CR3 helpers. This budget review is not a complete privileged-call audit.

Current installed GDT construction returns three descriptors and leaks heap backing for retention; IDT is separately installed. These are not an implemented user/TSS/emergency-entry resource set. Opaque host/source frame layouts do not establish hardware entry sizes or headroom.

virtual_geometry_and_guards.arena: Candidate 0x40000000..0x40400000 is 4194304 bytes / 1024 page slots, one aligned directory region. Validate actual active-map/reservation conflicts and table availability; no silent relocation.
virtual_geometry_and_guards.safe_user_only_example: Payload slot at 0x40000000..0x40001000; one-page user stack at 0x403ff000..0x40400000; lower absent guard 0x403fe000..0x403ff000. These example positions instantiate the approved arena arrangement, not installed mappings or approval of an entry ESP.
virtual_geometry_and_guards.absent_guards: Guard pages consume virtual address slots but no physical frames when truly nonpresent. At least one lower guard per downward-growing user/transition/emergency stack is a bounded candidate reservation convention, not a proof against all overflows or nested failures. Required geometry/count depends on F2/F3. Do not count physical frames for absence, nor call reserved-but-present identity pages guards.
virtual_geometry_and_guards.important_compatibility_constraint: Do not put present supervisor transition/emergency leaves into the user arena simply to make one-table accounting easy: approved E says all other arena leaves absent. Privileged stacks must use separate supervisor ranges backed through existing retained tables under this 12-frame policy. Final F3 selected ranges, adjacency, accessibility, alignment, absent guards and aliases must be explicitly checked. If those ranges require another new table, the one-table cap rejects them; if allowing supervisor arena leaves is desired, obtain an explicit amendment rather than asserting it is already approved.
virtual_geometry_and_guards.identity_aliases: Physical frames may be scattered. A virtually contiguous four-page stack need not be physically contiguous, but needs an audited mapping in existing tables. An inherited writable identity alias does not automatically supply a guarded contiguous stack. The actual ESP/ESP0/emergency stack pointer must use a guarded supervisor span; no alias may accidentally restore access to a guard at that span. Other supervisor-only physical aliases are separate from CPL3 permissions and must remain retained/audited.
virtual_geometry_and_guards.current_status: F1 does not create guards, and must label them unacquired/unmapped/unready reservations. No existing working guarded-stack installation is certified by this review.

metadata_and_existing_storage_policy.existing_retention: Retain existing directory/CR3, all installed boot table frames, PageMap table-vector/payload-bitmap/permanent-pin backing, allocator ledger, bootstrap kernel stack, boot inventory/heap storage and GDT/IDT backing separately. Record actual identities/counts at preparation; they are not zero memory just because incremental frame count is zero. Preserve their backing through terminal observation.
metadata_and_existing_storage_policy.minimal_fixed_metadata_shape: Use one const-initialized private owner, one monotonic attempt latch/state, one fixed resource-class manifest, bounded optional per-frame identity/lease slots covering at most the manifest's twelve frame roles (table role may remain in the private existing PageMap inventory), fixed range/readiness records for the three stack classes, one directory/domain identity, and scalar diagnostics. No Vec, dynamic bitmap, retry queue, per-event log or returned callback/guard/lease. Every concrete field and padding must be accounted in target ELF evidence; this is a structural bound, not an invented target byte size.
metadata_and_existing_storage_policy.future_descriptors: Use one fixed retained descriptor/TSS set for the selected CPU mechanism and, only if its reviewed mechanism requires it, a fixed additional emergency set within an explicitly amended/declared static shape. Do not assume a particular TSS byte count, task gate or emergency mechanism from this review. F2/F3 must select the architecture and reject incompatible resource requirements. Static descriptor growth is additional .data/.bss/allocated-span cost, not part of the twelve frame allocations.
metadata_and_existing_storage_policy.diagnostics: A fixed single terminal capture record with explicitly enumerated scalar fields and bounded direct output, no heap or locks after seal, is sufficient as a policy shape. Its actual fields, storage bytes and emitted handler stack use require F2/F3 verification. No claim of bounded total metadata is complete if future code may add unconstrained buffers or heap storage outside this declaration.
metadata_and_existing_storage_policy.f1_acceptance_gate: Before claiming implemented F1 boundedness, enumerate the actual fixed F1 owner fields, observe target static size/section deltas and preparation prologues against baseline, and account separately for unchanged preexisting resources. Future descriptor/diagnostic shapes may be uninstalled but must be finite declared shapes or explicit future integration rejection gates. A two-frame maximum alone cannot satisfy the whole retained-inventory contract.
metadata_and_existing_storage_policy.unknowns: Exact new owner size, future descriptor/capture byte sizes, target emitted frames, aggregate caller/IRQ/NMI/DF high-water and minimum-RAM deltas are unknown here. No build/test was permitted. These unknowns are not substituted by host type sizes or reviewer approval.

concrete_bounded_path: 1. Parent explicitly adopts/reviews a new policy manifest, distinguishing max eventual incremental frames, max actual F1 frames, fixed metadata shapes, retained baseline resources and absent virtual guards. Revise the provisional design's sufficiency-versus-ceiling ambiguity; do not claim B19 already approved the numbers.

2. Implement/test the retention mechanism only after the independently assigned boundary audit closes every reachable mutation/release bypass. Claim one attempt before any fallible acquisition. No IRQ ownership, lock-held formatting/allocation/destruction or exported owner authority; preserve heap -> map -> frame ordering.

3. In the F1-only controlled boot, acquire at most one payload and one sentinel frame. Retain every acquired lease before fallible validation. Validate domain/directory and effective writable supervisor identity aliases without modifying payload bytes. Any missing prerequisite/OOM/alias error is terminal and retry is forbidden; failure does not require a false successful-seal label.

4. On F1 success freeze the allocator/map domain irreversibly and exercise exact nonmutating refusal paths, including release/unmap/reset/growth/CR3 writes and retry, with same CR3 and bounded actual frame deltas. End this dedicated fixture terminally; do not return to a heap-using shell or attempt later preparation in that boot. CPL3 and CPU-ready flags remain false.

5. Future separately authorized revisions insert F2/F3/F4 work inside Preparing on a fresh boot. Revalidate the complete fixed manifest and checked actual selected ranges/tables, obtain required stack/architecture evidence, retain partial failures, then seal once. All allocation, PTE/guard publication and any prohibited CR3-writing helper must occur before seal; F4 cannot reuse current mutation helpers after it. CPU publication uses only the reviewed retained set, not a bypass to allocate/modify mappings.

6. F2/F3 must reject inadequate stacks, invalid CPU frame assumptions, missing independent emergency containment or excess metadata/tables even when every F1 policy test passes. F4 must reject cap/range conflicts and report actual frame identities/partial retained counts. F5 remains blocked until authoritative architecture, emitted code and actual CPU evidence close all entry obligations.

explicit_blockers_and_stop_conditions.condition: Any reachable allocator/map/release/reset/pin/CR3 mutation bypass, unknown actual per-attempt acquisition ceiling, or unbounded metadata/failure path. Whole-domain freeze feasibility is not proven by this budget review.

Trying to acquire/map/install guards after two-frame seal is incompatible. Must stop, never add unseal or a privileged post-seal mutation exemption. Fresh-boot source integration may extend Preparing, not Sealed.

No verified privileged-stack selected ranges/guard geometry fitting existing tables yet. One new arena table is a conditional admission cap, not proof of an installable full manifest. Extra required table/stack/context backing rejects this candidate.

Pinned architecture/CPU feature model, emitted ABI and cumulative stack/headroom/emergency containment evidence absent. Existing 16 KiB bootstrap reservation and tiny blob cannot replace them. Reviewer votes cannot create architecture correctness.
Candidate numbers and provisional owner design were not approved or implemented at snapshot. This conditional budget recommendation does not authorize source changes, acceptance execution or CPL3.

verification.hash_method: SHA-256 of Path.read_bytes(), no newline normalization. Computed frame/arena arithmetic with Python. Sources read in bounded relevant ranges, not a full-source architectural/caller audit.
verification.unrelated_files: Unchanged by this reviewer; no assumptions about their writer or meaning.
